ideas.pitch: A defense-in-depth security proxy and sanitizer designed to intercept and neutralize prompt injections and jailbreak attempts targeting RAG systems.
ideas.title: PromptGuard RAG
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly addresses the primary skill tested in Round 1 (LLM Jailbreak) by providing an architectural defense against the exact attack vectors judges will appreciate.

ideas.pitch: An AI-powered NGINX and access log analysis dashboard featuring automated anomaly detection for real-time security incident response during a CTF.
ideas.title: LogAnomalizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages proven patterns from cybersecurity hackathons by combining log parsing with automated threat detection, making it immediately useful for the offline CTF round.

ideas.pitch: A multi-agent network attack simulation and visualization tool that maps out lateral movement and vulnerability paths across a mock enterprise network.
ideas.title: GraphGuard CTF
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves technically difficult multi-agent orchestration and graph intelligence problems that consistently win security hackathons.

ideas.pitch: A BERT-powered multimodal spam and phishing detection system analyzing inbound emails, SMS, and webhook payloads for malicious payloads.
ideas.title: SpamShield AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows a proven runner-up blueprint from cyber hackathons by applying fine-tuned transformer models to practical social engineering threats.

ideas.pitch: A zero-knowledge gated community interface where human operators and AI agents can collaboratively exchange secret keys and CTF flags without exposing raw tokens.
ideas.title: AgentSecret Vault
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines advanced cryptography concepts with AI agents, hitting the technical depth bar required for top-tier competitive hacking events.
